name: Jeff Sessions
current_role: Former U.S. Attorney General (2017–2018) and former U.S. Senator from Alabama (1997–2017)
summary: Jeff Sessions is an Alabama Republican who served as U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Alabama, Alabama attorney general, U.S. senator from 1997 to 2017, and the 84th U.S. Attorney General from 2017 to 2018. He was the first senator to endorse Donald Trump in 2016, but his recusal from the Russia investigation led to a public rift; he resigned at Trump's request in November 2018 and lost the 2020 Alabama Senate Republican runoff to the Trump-endorsed Tommy Tuberville. A 1986 nomination to the federal bench was rejected by the Senate Judiciary Committee.

connections.name: Steve Bannon
connections.description: Bannon, then Breitbart News executive chairman, tried to recruit Sessions to run for president in 2013, called him a mentor, and is reported to have urged him to endorse Trump in February 2016. Breitbart defended Sessions during his attorney general confirmation.

connections.name: David Horowitz
connections.description: Sessions accepted the David Horowitz Freedom Center's 2014 Annie Taylor Award for Courage and credited Horowitz's writing with influencing his thinking. At his 2017 attorney general confirmation hearing he called Horowitz "a brilliant writer" while saying he was not comfortable with some of his language, and conceded he should have disclosed the award. Horowitz publicly objected to Trump's 2017 attacks on Sessions, and says he recommended Stephen Miller to him.

source_conflicts.details: Justice Department lawyers who had worked with Sessions testified that he made racially charged remarks; Sessions denied the allegations. The Republican-controlled Judiciary Committee voted 10–8 against advancing the nomination.
